hero.name: Tanushree Harika
roles: Learning DSA one problem at a time
hero.bio: IT student who builds things to learn things. From eye blink sensors to AI resume matchers — I figure it out as I go. Currently exploring Python, APIs, and whatever looks interesting next.

bioParas: I'm a B.Tech 2nd year IT student who got into coding by building random things and Googling my way through errors. That's still how I learn — pick something, build it, figure it out.
I've built an eye blink sensor, a job-matching AI, contributed to my department website, and survived my first hackathon. Not an expert at anything yet — but genuinely curious about everything.

softSkills.title: Communication
softSkills.note: Clear, confident & easy to talk to — genuinely my strongest suit.

softSkills.title: Curiosity
softSkills.note: I learn by building. If it looks interesting, I try it.

softSkills.title: Collaboration
softSkills.note: Worked with teams in hackathons & department projects.

softSkills.title: Persistence
softSkills.note: I don't give up — even when the bug makes no sense.

leetcode.description: Not crushing it yet, but I show up. Every problem teaches me to think better — and that's the whole point right now.

projects.title: Job Matching AI
projects.desc: Upload your resume and get matched to relevant job listings. Built to learn API integration, file handling, and working with a real backend stack — FastAPI + SQLite.

projects.title: Eye Blink Sensor
projects.desc: A hardware + software project that detects eye blinks in real time. Fun to build, surprisingly tricky to get right — learned a lot about sensors and signal processing.

projects.title: Department Website
projects.desc:
Contributed to my IT department's official website. Small contribution, but it taught me how real codebases work — reading others' code, making clean PRs, and collaborating properly..... 

website link https://vits-it-alumni-portal.vercel.app

experience.desc: Jumped into my first hackathon, built something under pressure with a team, and walked away with way more than I expected — mostly in terms of what I didn't know yet.
Made a small contribution to our department's website. Less about the code, more about learning how to work in a real codebase — reading PRs, understanding structure, not breaking things.

experience.company: Vignan Institute of Technology & Science  · Hyderabad
experience.desc: 2nd year IT student. Spending time in class, more time on personal projects, and even more time on Stack Overflow. Slowly connecting the dots between what I learn and what I build.
